AFFILIATION AGREEMENT AFFILIATION AGREEMENT BETWEEN: The University of Rhode Island on behalf of its Department of Nutrition and Food Sciences (hereafter referred to as the "University") And Sodexo Operations, LLC (hereafter referred to as “Sodexo").
I.
PURPOSE OF AGREEMENT The parties wish to collaborate for the purpose of enabling the University, with the assistance of Sodexo, to offer a masters-level graduate degree program in dietetics at the University to be known as The University of Rhode Island - Sodexo Future Graduate Dietetics Program (here in after to be referred to as the “Graduate Program'), as described herein and to be delivered in accordance with the terms and obligations of this Agreement and the Scope of Work in Appendix 1 attached hereto.
II.
COMMENCEMENT This Agreement shall commence on August 31, 2022 and shall be automatically renewed each year upon the anniversary of said commencement date (the “Renewal Date') and shall continue for a maximum of ten (1o) years, unless sooner terminated by either party in accordance with the terms herein.
Upon expiration of the Agreement, any additional term extensions shall be mutually agreed upon in writing by the parties.

Either party may terminate this Agreement by serving upon the other party a written notice, of not less than 90 days, in advance of the Renewal Date.
IH.
INSURANCE, INDEMNIFICATION and LIMITATION OF LIABILITY Insurance Throughout the entire term of the Agreement, each party shall maintain commercial general liability insurance covering their activities under this Agreement, in amounts of at least One Million Dollars ($1,000,000) per incident and Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000) in the coverage via electronic (email) distribution to an address designated by University.
All students participating in the Graduate Program who are enrolled as students at the University will be covered by the University's aforementioned commercial liability insurance.
All students participating in the Graduate Program who are also employed by Sodexo, or obtaining supervised experiential learning in dietetics provided by Sodexo shall likewise be covered by Sodexo's aforementioned commercial liability insurance.
Indemnification by Sodexo: Sodexo expressly agrees to indemnify, hold harmless, and defend at Sodexo's own cost and expense, the University and its governing board (and its members), as well as its 1

officers, employees, agents, and students (here in after (*University In dem nite es") against any and all claims or actions, and resulting damages or liabilities resulting from Sodexo's material breach of its obligations under this Agreement, or from the negligence or wrongful conduct of Sodexo or any of its employees, agents, representatives or contractors Indemnification by URI: The University expressly agrees to indemnify, hold harmless and defend at the University's own cost and expense, Sodexo, their agents, servants, and employees ("Sodexo In dem nite es") against any and all claims or actions, and resulting damages or liabilities, resulting from the University's material breach of its obligations under this Agreement, or from the negligence or wrongful conduct of the University or any of its employees, agents, representatives or contractors.
IV.

SOD EXO PERSONNEL participate in the Graduate Program and the supervised experiential learning in dietetics provided by Sodexo pursuant to this Agreement shall at all times, and for all purposes, be considered employees of Sodexo, and the only privileges that shall be extended by the University to such individuals shall be those that are explicitly set forth in this Agreement or that are routinely extended to the University's enrolled graduate students.
It is further understood that students participating in the Graduate Program may be, but need not be, employees of Sodexo, and such have the status of student interns at Sodexo.
V.
ASSIGNMENT AND GOVERNING LAW This Agreement or any part thereof shall not be assigned without the prior written consent of the other party.
Any attempted assignment without the aforementioned consent shall render this Agreement null and void.
This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Rhode Island, without regard for that state's choice of law principles.
VI.

DISCRIMINATION No person shall, on the grounds of race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, handicap, age, or national origin, be excluded from participation in, denied the benefits of, or be subject to discrimination under the terms of this Agreement.
The parties agree to comply with the provisions of all applicable laws and regulations, State and Federal, including but not limited to General Laws of Rhode Island 40.1-24 as amended, Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, Executive Order No. 85-11 on Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action, and all applicable rules and regulations issued there under.
The parties further agree to safeguard information in accordance with 45 CFR 228.10.
All services shall be provided without such discrimination.

VII.
CONFIDENTIALITY The parties shall generally keep the terms of this Agreement confidential, but each party may share the agreement and its terms, on a reasonable need to know basis with its ac creditors, insurers, attorneys and other parties with whom the party has a need to share the information.

Appendix 1 SCOPE OF WORK Scope of Workfor the University of Rhode Island - Sodexo Future Graduate Dietetics Program (the “Graduate Program") Program Name and Official Address University of Rhode Island - Sodexo Future Graduate Dietetics Program (the “Graduate Program") Department of Nutrition and Food Sciences University of Rhode Island 120 Ranger Hall Kingston, RI 02881 Collaborating Organizations URI and Sodexo will serve as collaborating organizations for the Graduate Program Brief Description of the Graduate Program The Graduate Program will be accredited by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND) to provide the education and experiential learning requirements for students to become Registered Dietitians.
URI will provide the didactic requirements culminating in a MS degree in Dietetics, and Sodexo will provide the required minimum of 1,000 hours of supervised experiential learning.
Responsibilities of the University of Rhode Island The responsibilities of the University of Rhode Island are to: Provide the Graduate Program Director who meets the requirements of URI and the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND).

The Graduate Program Director will have a 50% time allocation to administer the Graduate Program.
The Graduate Program Director will be responsible for overall management of the Graduate Program following ACEND and URI guidelines.
Provide all of the responsibilities required in the ACEND Standards for a Graduate Program Provide all didactic and practicum courses and course instructors (with the exception of the required “supervised experiential learning” activities to be provided by Sodexo in connection with their own independent, longstanding “Dietetic Internship Program", and as described below) for the Graduate Program culminating in a MS degree in Dietetics and fulfilling ACEND competencies.
A minimum of 75% of the student's time or credit hours will be at the University. ·Confer the degree and maintain student records. 5

· Provide the ACEND verification statement upon Graduate Program completion and maintain these statements indefinitely. ·Assess prior learning of students upon entry to the Graduate Program. · Provide the resources needed to offer the MS degree including administrative/clerical support, IT support, facilities, and student support services.
Develop and market the Graduate Program to potential students.
Share data with the Sodexo co-Director, following FERPA guidelines, to ensure that students successfully complete the experiential learning component of the Graduate Program and to submit accreditation documentation.
Responsibilities of the Sodexo Corporation The responsibilities of the Sodexo Corporation are to: · Provide the Graduate Program Co-Director to manage supervised experiential learning. ·Provide preceptors for supervised experiential learning.
Provide a minimum of 1,0o0 hours of supervised experiential learning activities for each student to meet ACEND competencies.
Provide the resources needed for supervised experiential learning including administrative/clerical support, IT support, facilities, and student support services.
Participate in writing of all ACEND required reports.

Share data with the Graduate Program Director, following FERPA guidelines, to ensure that the Graduate Program can assign grades, confer degrees, and submit accreditation documentation.
Other requirements set forth in the Affiliation Agreement Have full legal and administrative responsibility for all aspects of the supervised experiential learning in dietetics at Sodexo, including responsibility for the collection of all Sodexo tuition and other fees from students, and the maintenance of all appropriate policies and procedures for the experiential learning, and adherence to all applicable laws, including federal and state labor laws, relating to the supervised experiential learning in dietetics at Sodexo.
Exclusivity Agreement dietetics only through the Sodexo supervised experiential learning in dietetics.
Sodexo, however, shall be entitled to train students enrolled in other programs with client partners other than URI.
Financial Management ·Each Collaborating Organization will charge its own tuition and fees, and this money will be used to pay its individual costs.
Neither Collaborating Organization is responsible for paying any costs incurred by the other Collaborating Organization.
Each Collaborating Organization will equally share in the accreditation fees (annual fee and the self-study/site visit fee) of the Graduate Program. 6

Teach Out Process If the Graduate Program is dissolved, or the Affiliation Agreement is terminated by either party, the Collaborating Organizations agree to teach out any students remaining in the Graduate Program so that students can complete the Graduate Program within 150% of the Graduate Program length. Since the Graduate Program length is 14 months, the teach out process will be concluded by 21months.

If a Policy Owner concludes that a policy within its oversight has no continuing applicability , the Policy Owner may propose retirement of the policy through the same review and approval channels set forth above for approval of policies.
Retired Academic Policies shall be incorporated into archived versions of the University Manual.
Retired Administrative Policies will be archived but accessible from the University Policy Website (www.uri.edu/policies).
Additional Information Nothing in this policy limits the authority of the University to issue, amend, or withdraw a policy.
Exceptions None

THE UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND Revised 8/2016 Notice of Change form Notice of Change for: URI CON PMHNP Specialty Track in the MS Program and the Post-MS Certificate Program Date: October 7, 2021 A. PROGRAM INFORMATION 1. Name of institution University of Rhode Island 2. Name of department, division, school or college Department: Graduate Nursing College: College of Nursing 3. Intended initiation date of program change. Include anticipated date for granting first degrees or certificates, if appropriate. Initiation date: Sept 2022 First degree date: May 2024 4. Intended location of the program URI College of Nursing Graduate Program Nursing Education Center 350 Eddy St. Providence, RI 02903 5. Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages). The College of Nursing offers 3 nurse practitioner (NP) specialty tracks within its MS program and its Post-MS Certificate Program. These include Adult-Gerontology Primary Care NP, Family NP and Psychiatric-Mental Health NP (PMHNP). The first two of these specialties focus on primary care and are identical in terms of total credits in the MS Program (42) and very similar in terms of coursework and other program requirements. The PMHNP specialty track is the newest specialty track offered within the MS program

2 and currently requires 48 - 49 credits.
Having just graduated their first few graduates in the PMHNP specialty track, the PMHNP program faculty, the MS/DNP Program Committee and Associate Dean Kathy Hutchinson all agreed that revisions were needed within the PMHNP specialty track to address 3 issues.
The 3 issues and proposed changes to the PMHNP specialty track are outlined below and shown in Appendix A: (1) the credit allocations for some of the courses within the PMHNP specialty (e.g., NUR 545) needed to be corrected to be more consistent with university standards and other course offerings within the program.
NUR 545 focuses on psychiatric-mental health care for children, adolescents and families and is a 2 credit course.
In contrast, NUR 513 focuses on psychiatric-mental health care for adults and is a 3 credit course.

The didactic NP specialty courses in the other NP specialty tracks are all 3 credit courses. (2) In addition to correcting the inconsistency in credit allocations to didactic courses, the faculty and MS/DNP cmte. sought to address uneven distribution of clinical practicum credits across the PMHNP clinical courses (NUR 514, 546 and 547) and align these credits with those in the other NP specialty tracks.
The current PMHNP specialty requires 500- 600+ clinical hours and the 3 clinical courses total 15 credits.
In comparison, the other specialty tracks require similar clinical hours but allocate only 12 credits across their 3 clinical courses. (3) In order to be consistent with recommendations from our accrediting body (The American Association of Colleges of Nursing / CCNE), the CON implemented a single course addressing Advanced Health Assessment / Physical Assessment Across the Lifespan (NUR 530) In Fall, 2021.
This 4 credit didactic and lab course will now be completed by students in all 3 nurse practitioner specialty tracks in the MS program.
In the past, PMHNP students took an abbreviated 3 credit course in health assessment (NUR 501).

This change alone would result in an additional 1 credit increase to the PMHNP track of the MS curriculum.
The number of credits for this specialty track is already high.
Addressing the issues in (1) and (3) above would result in a 1 - 2 credit increase in the number of credits in the PMHNP specialty track.
Balancing this against the need to reduce clinical credits in (2) above, would result in an overall reduction in the number of credits for the PMHNP specialty track in the MS program from 48-49 to 47.
The individual course syllabi have been revised to reflect changes in pre-requisites (NUR 530 replaces NUR 501 as a pre-requisite for all the specialty courses [e.g., NUR 513, 514, 545, 546 and 547]).
The course descriptions have been clarified and the course objectives reviewed and edited slightly.
The descriptions for the clinical practicum courses (NUR 514, 546, 547) have been abbreviated and written more broadly to indicate that these courses focus on the application of previous and concurrent learning in a variety of practice settings.

3 These proposed changes to the PMHNP Specialty Track of the MS program result in minor changes to the PMHNP Specialty Track of the Post-MS Certificate Program, specifically a redistribution of credits across the PMHNP courses (NUR 502, 513, 514, 545, 546) as was described above. The total number of credits for the PMHNP Post-Master’s Certificate will remain at 20 credits. 6. Jessica Strubel, COB (2022) UM Chapter 8: Centers and Institutes Recommended Language: 8.90.20 Procedures for the Establishment of Centers and Institutes.
Proposals for all centers and institutes shall originate with faculty representing the disciplines concerned.
A proposal for the creation of a center or institute shall include an explanation of its goals and rationale, a description of its proposed administrative and staffing structure, a specific description of its relationship to other appropriate

units of the University, a budget with personnel and space requirements, as well as amounts and sources of seed money.
A template for the application can be obtained from the Center Review Subcommittee (CRS) of the Faculty Senate Research and Creative Activities Committee (RCAC).
Proposals are judged based on program quality, research, outreach, or educational activities, involvement of undergraduate and graduate students, interdepartmental or intercollege connections, and potential for continued financial viability, as appropriate for the mission and goals of the center or institute.
Any specific arrangements for space, staff, financial support, or overhead return agreed to by the college, department or Vice President for Research and Economic Development should be documented in the application.
Applications approved by RCAC will be presented to the Faculty Senate for a vote prior to forwarding the application to the Vice President for Research and Economic Development and the Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs for final approval. #11-12–25, #17-18-23 #20-21-32 8.90.30 Review.

Centers and institutes shall be reviewed every four years by the Center Review Subcommittee (CRS) of the Research and Creative Activities Committee (RCAC).
Additionally, continuing authorization to operate centers or institutes may be subject to review by units and departments involved in the center or institute as well as review by the colleges of the involved departments.
A reporting template for the review can be obtained from the RCAC.
College reviews, if applicable, can be submitted as support documentation with this template.
Successful completion of the review will be based on overall program quality, research, outreach, or educational contributions, financial support, student involvement, interdepartmental or intercollege involvement, and continued external funding financial viability, as appropriate for the mission and goals of the center or institute.
The review of center’s and institute’s activities will be included in the RCAC’s report to the Faculty Senate annually.
Centers and institutes can be dissolved willingly by their leadership.
